arxiv-2008-06991.title: In-situ Workflow Auto-tuning via Combining Performance Models of Component Applications Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2008-06991.creator: Tong Shu, Yanfei Guo, Justin Wozniak, Xiaoning Ding, Ian Foster, Tahsin Kurc
arxiv-2008-06991.description: Abstract . In-situ parallel workflows couple multiple component applications, such as simulation and analysis, via streaming data transfer in order to avoid data exchange via shared file systems. Such workflows are challenging to configure for optimal performance due to the large space of possible configurations.

arxiv-2208-06412.title: Contrastive Learning for Object Detection
arxiv-2208-06412.creator: Rishab Balasubramanian Kunal Rathore
arxiv-2208-06412.description: Abstract 1 Introduction 1.1 Problem Statement In this project we will be working on Object Detection using Contrastive Learning. The goal of the project is to implement and evaluate the success of contrastive learning paradigm for learning better feature representations, and use these for object detection.

arxiv-2212-08464.title: Free-form 3D Scene Inpainting with Dual-stream GAN
arxiv-2212-08464.creator: Ru-Fen Jheng, Tsung-Han Wu, Jia-Fong Yeh, Winston H. Hsu
arxiv-2212-08464.description: Abstract Nowadays, the need for user editing in a 3D scene has rapidly increased due to the development of AR and VR technology. However, the existing 3D scene completion task (and datasets) cannot suit the need because the missing regions in scenes are generated by the sensor limitation or object occlusion.

arxiv-2401-07654.title: Foundation Models for Biomedical Image Segmentation: A Survey
arxiv-2401-07654.creator: Ho Hin Lee*, Yu Gu*, Theodore Zhao, Yanbo Xu, Jianwei Yang, Naoto Usuyama, Cliff Wong, Mu Wei
arxiv-2401-07654.description: Abstract Recent advancements in biomedical image analysis have been significantly driven by the Segment Anything Model (SAM). This transformative technology, originally developed for general-purpose computer vision, has found rapid application in medical image processing. Within the last year, marked by over 100 publications, SAM has demonstrated its prowess in zero-shot learning adaptations for medical imaging.

arxiv-2410-16027.title: ComPO : Community Preferences for Language Model Personalization
arxiv-2410-16027.creator: Sachin Kumar, Chan Young Park, Yulia Tsvetkov, Noah A. Smith, Hannane Hajishirzi
arxiv-2410-16027.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sachin Kumar, Chan Young Park, Yulia Tsvetkov, Noah A. Smith, Hannane Hajishirzi. Conventional algorithms for training language models (LMs) with human feedback rely on preferences that are assumed to account for an “average” user, disregarding subjectivity and finer-grained variations. Recent studies have raised concerns that aggregating such diverse and often contradictory human feedback to finetune models results in generic models that generate outputs not preferred by many users groups, as they tend to average out styles and norms.

arxiv-2503-19474.title: A-MESS: Anchor-based Multimodal Embedding with Semantic Synchronization for Multimodal Intent Recognition
arxiv-2503-19474.creator: Yaomin Shen 1 * , Xiaojian Lin 2 , Wei Fan 3 , 1 XR System Application Research Center, Nanchang Research Institute, Zhejiang University, China 2 Institute for AI Industry Research(AIR), Tsinghua University, China 3 Independent Researcher, China 1 coolshennf@gmail.com, 2 chrislim@connect.hku.hk, 3 c
arxiv-2503-19474.description: Abstract In the domain of multimodal intent recognition (MIR), the objective is to recognize human intent by integrating a variety of modalities, such as language text, body gestures, and tones. However, existing approaches face difficulties adequately capturing the intrinsic connections between the modalities and overlooking the corresponding semantic representations of intent.

arxiv-2504-04541.title: A model agnostic eXplainable AI based fuzzy framework for sensor constrained Aerospace maintenance applications
arxiv-2504-04541.creator: Bharadwaj Dogga*, Anoop Sathyan, and Kelly Cohen
arxiv-2504-04541.description: Abstract Machine Learning methods have extensively evolved to support industrial big data methods and their corresponding need in gas turbine maintenance and prognostics. However, most unsupervised methods need extensively labeled data to perform predictions across many dimensions. The cutting edge of small and medium applications do not necessarily maintain operational sensors and data acquisition with rising costs and diminishing profits.

arxiv-2505-13236.title: Multiple-Order Tensor Field Theory: Enumeration of unitary invariant observables
arxiv-2505-13236.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . In Tensor Field Theory (TFT), observables are defined through tensor field contractions that produce unitary invariants for complex-valued tensor fields. Traditionally, these observables are constructed using tensor fields of a fixed order d d . Here, we propose an extended theoretical framework for TFT that incorporates tensor fields of varying orders d ′ d^{\prime} , satisfying d ′ ≤ d d^{\prime}\leq d . We then establish a comprehensive group-theoretic formalism that enables the systematic enumeration of these complex TFT observables.

pmc-11504861.title: Increased Susceptibility to Mechanical Stretch Drives the Persistence of Keloid Fibroblasts: An Investigation Using a Stretchable PDMS Platform
pmc-11504861.creator: Jihee Kim, Chihyeong Won, Seoyoon Ham, Heetak Han, Sungsik Shin, Jieun Jang, Sanghyeon Lee, Chaebeen Kwon, Sungjoon Cho, Hyeonjoo Park, Dongwon Lee, Won Jai Lee, Taeyoon Lee, Ju Hee Lee
pmc-11504861.description: Background: Keloids are a common fibrotic disease of the skin, with the pathological hallmark of excessive extracellular matrix synthesis due to abnormal fibroblast activity. Since keloids clinically arise in areas of high mechanical tension, the mechanotransductory pathway may be attributed to its pathogenesis.

pmc-11642066.title: Small Diameter (7.5 Fr) Single-Use Flexible Ureteroscopy with Direct In-Scope Suction (DISSTM) in Conjunction with Aspiration-Assisted Flexible Access Sheath: A New Hype for Real Stone-Free?
pmc-11642066.creator: Petrișor Geavlete, Cristian Mareș, Răzvan Mulțescu, Dragoș Georgescu, Cosmin-Victor Ene, Valentin Iordache, Bogdan Geavlete, Magdi Yaqoob
pmc-11642066.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Renal lithiasis continues to represent a great challenge for modern urology in terms of minimally invasive management of lithotripsy procedures. The recent revolution of endoscopes with the miniaturization of instruments and the development of improved disposable ureteroscopes combined with recent suction methods such as suction access sheaths or direct in-scope suction (DISSTM) systems promise to further improve the outcome of renal stone treatment.

pmc-11649140.title: Level of health literacy and associated factors among Jimma town public high school adolescent students: A cross-sectional study
pmc-11649140.creator: Merga Garoma Jatu, Desalew Tilahun Beyene, Dechasa Befikadu W. Senbat, Tesfaye Asfaw Alemayehu, Diribsa Tizazu Hailu, Serkalem Aschalew Jima, Midhagsaa Dhinsa Kitila, Ebissa Bayana Kebede
pmc-11649140.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to assess the level of health literacy and its associated factors among Jimma town public high school adolescents, Jimma, Oromia, Southwest Ethiopia, 2023.MethodsA facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted in June 2023 among 604 Jimma town public high school adolescents. A multistage sampling technique was employed to recruit study participants.

pmc-11654069.title: Association between ZJU index and gallstones in US adult: a cross-sectional study of NHANES 2017–2020
pmc-11654069.creator: Zuopu Xie, Xianpei Chen, Chunming Xie, Qi Yang, Hao Lin
pmc-11654069.description: BackgroundBased on triglyceride, body mass index (BMI), alanine aminotransferase/ aspartate aminotransferase ratio, fasting blood glucose, the ZJU index is proven to be a novel and effective parameter for screening NAFLD in Chinese. This study aims to evaluate the correlation between ZJU values and the risk of developing gallstones.

pmc-12571413.title: The effect of education with WhatsApp application on women's health beliefs, self-efficacy levels, and regular mammography behavior: a randomized controlled experimental trial
pmc-12571413.creator: Hasret Yalçınöz Baysal, Sonay Bilgin, Abdullah Baysal, Selen Özdemir, Kemal Yaran, Gülsüm Aşan
pmc-12571413.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:The aim of this study was to determine the effect of the Health Belief Model-based training provided to women via WhatsApp on their health beliefs about mammography, self-efficacy levels, and regular mammography behavior.METHODS:This randomized controlled experimental trial was conducted with 81 women (41 experimental and 40 control), aged 40–69 years, who were literate, able to use WhatsApp, and had no communication barriers, and had no history of breast cancer.

pmc-12653070.title: The Influence of Nitrogen on Culturable Phyllosphere Microorganisms and the Incidence of Botrytis cinerea in Postharvest Leafy Vegetables
pmc-12653070.creator: Viktorija Vaštakaitė-Kairienė, Darius Jermala, Alma Valiuškaitė, Kristina Bunevičienė, Armina Morkeliūnė, Neringa Rasiukevičiūtė, Lucia Landi
pmc-12653070.description: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa), pak choi (Brassica rapa), and basil (Ocimum basilicum) were grown in hydroponic NFT systems under four nitrate levels (80–180 mg L−1 N). We measured natural microbial contamination by plating nutrient-solution samples and leaf washes to obtain colony-forming unit (CFU) counts of bacteria and fungi.

pmc-12831397.title: TP53 mutations as drivers of chordoma progression and hallmarks of aggressive chordoma
pmc-12831397.creator: Szymon Baluszek, Paulina Kober, Michał Wa̧grodzki, Jacek Kunicki, Bartosz Wojtaś, Paulina Szadkowska, Bożena Kamińska, Thibault Passeri, Tomasz Mandat, Mateusz Bujko
pmc-12831397.description: IntroductionDedifferentiated (DC) and poorly differentiated chordomas (PDC) are rare, aggressive chordomas with a significantly worse prognosis than conventional chordomas (CC). The molecular mechanisms driving them remain poorly understood.MethodsMatched primary CC and recurrent DC cryopreserved samples from one patient were analyzed with whole-exome sequencing (WES). Samples from three additional DCs and one PDC underwent targeted sequencing of cancer-related genes.

pmc-12853788.title: Development of video exercise-based mobile application to improve the clinical outcomes in patients with knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12853788.creator: Fatih Özden, Baki Umut Tuğay, Osman Çoban, Barış Ethem Süzek, Nazan Tuğay, Zübeyir Sarı, İrem Çetinkaya, Gülser Cinbaz, İsmet Tümtürk
pmc-12853788.description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to develop a video exercise-based mobile application and investigate its effectiveness in terms of pain, function, expectation, and satisfaction in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA).MethodsA randomized controlled trial was carried out with 52 individuals with knee OA.

pmc-13339803.title: GRIA Gene Expression in Schizophrenia: A Participant-Level Meta-Analysis
pmc-13339803.creator: Adan Baumel, Assif Yitzhaky, Libi Hertzberg
pmc-13339803.description: Background:Schizophrenia is a complex mental disorder with an estimated heritability of 80%, yet its underlying pathophysiology remains poorly understood. Emerging evidence implicates the α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole propionic acid (AMPA) glutamate receptor—a key player in fast excitatory synaptic transmission, encoded by Glutamate Ionotropic Receptor AMPA Type Subunits 1-4 (GRIA1-4)—in the disorder's pathophysiology.

pmc-13360935.description: Beyond nutrition, taste quality is a key quality trait driving the global popularity of Agaricus bisporus. This study systematically investigated non-volatile taste-related metabolite dynamics in caps and stipes during fruiting body development using non-targeted metabolomics. Among 1358 identified metabolites (974 in caps, 997 in stipes), 328 taste-related metabolites were screened. Applying screening criteria of VIP > 1, p < 0.

pmc-13419686.title: Effect of ALDH2 rs671 and ADH1B rs1229984 polymorphisms on habitual alcohol use: evidence from a large Taiwanese cohort
pmc-13419686.creator: Mu-En Liu, Yu-Ting Yan, Yu-Tung Tien, Wei-Ming Liu, Ding-Lieh Liao, Po-Hsiu Kuo, Shih-Jen Tsai
pmc-13419686.description: BackgroundTwo functional genetic polymorphisms, ADH1B rs1229984 and ALDH2 rs671, play key roles in ethanol metabolism and are especially prevalent in East Asian populations. The rs1229984 variant accelerates the conversion of ethanol to acetaldehyde, whereas rs671 reduces enzymatic activity for converting acetaldehyde into acetic acid. These variants affect alcohol use disorder risk and have been implicated in various systemic conditions.

uslaw-usc-t28-s2077.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2077 — Publication of rules; advisory committees
uslaw-usc-t28-s2077.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2077.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part V (Procedure); Chapter 131 (Rules Of Courts). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The rules for the conduct of the business of each court of appeals, including the operating procedures of such court, shall be published. Each court of appeals shall print or cause to be printed necessary copies of the rules.
